extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research administrators, and institutions applying for or managing NIH extramural grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and managing NIH grant applications and awards, including required registrations, adherence to NIH policy documents, and compliance with federal grant administration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIHGPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting a grant award, recipients agree to comply with the requirements in the NIH Grants Policy Statement unless the notice of award states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIHGPS makes available, in a single document, the policy requirements that serve as the terms and conditions of NIH grant awards; applicants and awardees must follow the NIHGPS except where a Notice of Award indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and follow Notices of Policy Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices published in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts can supersede information in the NIH Grants Policy Statement and/or provide reminders to applicants and recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and recipients must track Notices of Policy Changes because NIH incorporates these notices into the annual update of the NIHGPS and notices may change applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand NIH structure and required registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain an understanding of key concepts like how the NIH structure impacts funding and how to get registered to do business with us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying, investigators and institutions should learn how NIH's organizational structure affects funding opportunities and complete any required registrations (e.g., entity registrations) needed to submit applications and receive awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the grants process steps (planning, submission, award, closeout)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about the steps required for an application to proceed from planning and submission through award and closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NIH procedures at each stage (planning, submission, review, award administration, and closeout) to ensure applications are properly processed and awards are managed in compliance with NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with federal requirements and proper use of grant funds (Compliance and Oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal requirements, guidelines and resources for the extramural community involving grants compliance are provided to assist in understanding the compliance obligations of their grant award and understanding the proper use of grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must meet applicable federal statutes, regulations, and NIH guidance governing use of funds, financial management, reporting, and oversight; institutions should consult NIH resources to understand obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biosketch is listed as a select policy topic; applicants must follow NIH biosketch format and content requirements as specified in NIH guidance and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of Other Support (financial and in-kind support) is a required policy topic; applicants and investigators must provide accurate Other Support information per NIH instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Common Forms and expect system enforcement (end of leniency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcement of Upcoming System Enforcement of Common Forms and End of NIH's Leniency Period
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will enforce use of required common forms via systems; applicants should prepare to submit using the mandated forms and cannot rely on prior leniency for nonconforming submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Uniform Administrative Requirements for Federal Financial Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Update - NIH Implementation of Uniform Administrative Requirements for Federal Financial Assistance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH implements the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR part 200) and related administrative requirements; applicants and recipients must follow these uniform administrative rules for federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to updated peer review practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of Modifications to Peer Review Practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH is modifying peer review practices; applicants should be aware of current review criteria and processes and prepare applications consistent with the updated expectations for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Transparency Act subaward reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of Transparency Act Subaward Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subaward reporting obligations under the Transparency Act may apply; recipients must ensure subawards are reported as required by the applicable policy and reporting systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow policies for Basic Experimental Studies with Humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of Changes for Basic Experimental Studies with Humans
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, investigators must follow NIH requirements specific to basic experimental studies involving human subjects, including any new or revised implementation details provided by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to NIH's late application submission policy and end of continuous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Update of NIH Late Application Submission Policy and End of Continuous Submission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow NIH's current late submission rules and note that continuous submission has ended; adherence to submission deadlines and procedures is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH's harmonized definition of Intervention consistent with the Common Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonizing the NIH Definition of Intervention with the Common Rule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH is aligning its definition of 'intervention' with the Common Rule; investigators should apply the harmonized definition when determining human subjects protections and related policy applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain prior approval for changes to domestic subawards
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior Approval Requirement for Changes to Domestic Subawards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain changes to domestic subawards require prior NIH approval; recipients must seek and obtain prior approval where specified before implementing such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track publication of revised NIH Grants Policy Statement (FY2026, Rev. March 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the Revised NIH Grants Policy Statement (Rev. March 2026) for Fiscal Year 2026
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH periodically revises the NIHGPS; applicants and recipients should consult the most recent NIHGPS (e.g., Rev. March 2026) for current terms and conditions that govern awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for modernized data and safety monitoring policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizing NIH Data and Safety Monitoring Policy Webinar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH intends to modernize data and safety monitoring approaches; applicants and institutions should monitor policy development, participate in public engagement when possible, and be ready to update monitoring plans to align with new policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan format (2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan Format Available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH published a pilot format for Data Management and Sharing Plans in 2026; applicants expected to prepare data management and sharing plans using the available pilot format where applicable.
